The South Carolina Department of Health and Environmental Control reported adverse effects on West Bad Creek, Bad Creek, and Howard Creek as a result of the construction of Highway 171.
The benthic community of Howard Creek is composed of macroinvertebrates typical of fast-flowing, digotrophic headwater streams. Aquatic insects dominate the community with Ephemeroptera (Mayflies), Diptera (true flies), Trichoptera (caddisflies), Plecoptera (stoneflies), and Coleoptera (beetles) totaling 98.6 percent by number of the organisms collected (in order of abundance). Stoneflies and caddisflies provide a major food source to lotic fishes, especially trout. The above groups include important trout stream organisms (Pennak, 1953).
